repo_notes.content: TA-Lib ships native implementations in C/C++, Rust (crates.io `ta-lib`), Java (Maven Central `io.github.ta-lib:ta-lib`) and C# (NuGet `TA-Lib`). The Rust, Java and C# libraries are written entirely in their own language: they use no JNI, no P/Invoke and no C library, and need nothing else installed. Python, R and other languages use wrappers around the C library, such as ta-lib-python.

Every function has a batch API (compute over an array, selected by startIdx/endIdx) and, since 0.8.1, a streaming API: open a stream on history, update it once per closed bar, and peek at a forming bar without changing its state. Document both forms in every language; never describe TA-Lib as array-only.

User documentation lives in website/src and is published at https://ta-lib.org; base user-facing pages on it rather than on inference from source code. ta_codegen/ (the generator that produces all four language implementations from one source), src/tools/ta_regtest, ta_ref/ and scripts/ are maintainer internals: cover them only under 'For Contributors'. Files named CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and README-DEVS.md are maintainer and agent instructions, not user documentation. The old gen_code.c generator, the JNI-based Java binding and the Managed C++ .NET wrapper no longer exist; do not describe them.
